_doc: Server-side only, as data (owner, 2026-11-12). Read by foundation/serverside.py: `python3 -m foundation serverside --check`, called from foundation/doctrine.py check() and so from the doctrine step of checks.yml. It fails a change that brings a person's computer back as a host, scheduler, agent or route. Prose is not the enforcement; this file is. Changed only by a reviewed PR.
rule: Server-side only (owner, 2026-11-12): Ultrastable runs server-side only. Nothing may assume, depend on or reference infrastructure on a person's computer: no scheduler there, no code agent there, no desktop app that must be open, no owner laptop. Every loop, merge, deploy and check runs on the infrastructure Ultrastable itself runs on: the Cloudflare worker `ultrastable-tick` with D1 `ultrastable-org`, GitHub Actions, and cloud-hosted agent routines.

cloudflare.what: the Cloudflare worker ultrastable-tick (cron) with D1 ultrastable-org

github-actions.what: GitHub Actions workflows in this repository; the built-in token is the credential no person mints

claude-cloud.what: a cloud-hosted Claude routine or session (scheduler, container and session on Anthropic's servers)

banned.why: the Windows scheduler runs on a person's computer
cron tables, systemd and launchd units are schedulers on a computer somebody owns and keeps on
a scheduled task of the desktop app runs only while that app is open; the server-side form is a cloud-hosted routine. Cloud scheduled tasks of any vendor are not matched
a host, agent, loop or route on a person's computer

banned.pattern: on the laptop|owner(['\u2019]s)? (machine|laptop|computer|pc)\b|[A-Za-z]:\\Users\\|desktop app (that )?(must|has to|needs to) be open
banned.why: names a particular person's computer or a path on it
an address that only means something on the computer it is typed on

banned.pattern: signed-in cli[^.\n]{0,40}(owner|person)'s (machine|computer)|machine's existing sign-in|local gh login
banned.why: a CLI sign-in found on a person's computer is not a credential route; the ladder accepts it only on a server-side host

excused_note: A line may name a banned thing only to state the rule, and then it cites the rule on the same line (the phrase 'server-side only'). Nothing else excuses a line.

skip_dirs.reason: git's own storage, not the tree
scratch databases written by the selfhost run, never committed
backup bundles of other repositories, not this system's code

the folded-in core kept in its standalone layout (REPOS-1): its local dev demos, SSRF guards that refuse localhost, and blocker cases that describe an unreachable owner computer name a person's computer as a thing to refuse, never as a host, scheduler or route; its own tests (cd workers && npm test) guard it

exclude.reason: the spun-off apps' Worker refuses loopback and private names as SSRF guards for the public domain a visitor types; it never connects to a person's computer
this file holds the banned patterns themselves
its removed ledger must name the deleted desktop task definition by its old path so the removal stays recoverable
patch files quote the removed lines of sibling repositories byte for byte; editing them breaks the patch
the loopback address is the Postgres service container inside the GitHub Actions runner, which is server-side
an in-memory adapter that exists as a test fixture; its comment describes in-process test runs, not a host
a dated incident log; its rows record failed attempts to reach a person's computer, which is the lesson the rule keeps
the directory refuses loopback and private names in a URL someone registers (SSRF guard, DISCOVER-1); it never connects to a person's computer
